title: Introduction to group
author: Ok-Way-9449
selftext:
I am a Baby Boomer Old Fart that loves technology, going back to the Commodore 64 and the Web since we had Netscape 1.0.   The first thing I did with AI is take a Tera Online emulator I had on my computer for a few years.  I used OpenCode with Big Pickle to start with.  The emulator was mostly Java except for the Client.  It was an Alpha version of Tera that had been released years ago so it was old school Tera.  I wanted to know how to change the NPC text and add a simple quest.   Ai helped me figure out everything on the server side very quickly.  The client had a different can of worms, it had to be unpacked and replaced, and you had to have a key for the version client you had.   I watched the AI for hours trying and find the key.    I finally got the Key from a Ragezone Tera board.   It unpacked it the file made a couple minor changes and tried to repack it.   The AI tried and tried to repack it.  I finally went to 2 other AI's and told it the problem we were having repacking and both gave possible fixes.  I copied and pasted their answers into OpenCode and BAM it worked.   I learned the hard way when you get a breakthrough with AI you have it create a file that any AI can read and do what it just did.  I was able to fix everything that was broken on the Island of Dawn including the missing Dungeon.  I had a lot of fun trying different things,

 

Now I am working on combining 2 of my favorite games together BattleHeart style play and combat and Tera Classes.   I use Codex, Claude and OpenCode.  I am on my 4th iteration of the game I get so far and study what I have and start over as it is not quite what I want.  For sprites I have used just about anything.  Co=Pilot to take a screen shot of a character and turn it into a Chibi BattleHeart style.   Ludo.ai to create sprites.  And when I could not get what I wanted looking right I would go into GROK Imagine having a Character walking video then upload the video to https://spritemaster.pages.dev/  Its free an spits out a sprite sheet.   I let Codex review the sprite sheet and pick the best frames for a simple sprite sheet and this process works well.  The current iteration is a Battle-Engine for all the code necessary to create a battle with waves of enemies.    As I have been developing this in Codex, I have Clause and Open Code review the project and give me their thoughts.  Any weak areas that need improvement I feed back to Codex.  The battle-engine is basically done, and I was working on an APK version, but my file size was getting way too big.  So I am currently changing all my sprites into Paperdoll models with rigging and just about done.  I have all the Battle Scenes worked out and the Game system and need to tune the enemy waveys and everyone’s HP Attack Power and Defense.

I look forward to reaing everyone's post.
